name: Stage Contrast
use: A decisive opening for live launches and short pitches.
cover: Put the key phrase beside one large, cropped image.
content: Pair a comparison with a numbered graphic. Keep captions in a uniform baseline.

name: Dark Current
use: Polished technical demos and business reviews.
cover: Offset a product image against a dim pool of light.
content: Repeat the same baseline in diagrams and annotation bars.

name: High-Energy Grid
use: Energetic studio work and event openers.
cover: Place large two-line words against a sparse oversize grid.
content: Build alternating side-by-side pairs for evidence and a single result.

name: Night Garden
use: Reflective fieldwork, personal talks and nature-oriented subjects.
cover: Rest the headline on a photo or a dark layered field.
content: Use an asymmetric photograph-and-story pairing with fine lines.

name: File Tabs
use: Warm lesson materials and practical process explanations.
cover: Expose one tab above a paper-like title region.
content: Use consistent tabs to compare steps and show session checkpoints.

name: Soft Shapes
use: An approachable teaching deck for first-time learners.
cover: Use a few large shapes behind the centered learning goal.
content: Reserve a quieter flat field for clear diagrams and labels.

name: Two-Color Field
use: Friendly announcements and paired comparisons.
cover: Balance two contrasting fields around the core message.
content: Group two conditions into matching structures with paired color cues.

name: Archive Editorial
use: Readouts with archival artifacts, quotations and portraits.
cover: Lead with a classic headline, clear context and one archival image.
content: Use narrow columns with marginal captions and dark rules.

name: Neon Vector
use: Futuristic announcements and live technical demos.
cover: Give the title a clean beam of color and angular stage marks.
content: Use small vivid marks to tag real changes and keep technical drawings on flat fields.

name: Console Green
use: Engineering tutorials and code-led technical reports.
cover: Set an uncluttered typographic prompt and one small status detail.
content: Align examples and diagrams to fixed columns. Use long code only when necessary.

name: Precise Grid
use: Precise reports and comparison-heavy talks.
cover: Align type to a disciplined left edge with one strong graphic mark.
content: Use strict columns, aligned numbers and narrow figure captions.

name: Quiet Paper
use: Reading-first reports with a calm editorial pace.
cover: Use one generous headline and a light rule.
content: Set body copy in readable measures and use a small caption scale only for sources.

name: Arcade Board
use: Pixel-era demonstrations and short creative talks.
cover: Frame the title with stepped pixels and a single real product visual.
content: Use chunky marks around short numeric cues and keep explanatory type simple.

name: Ochre Wall
use: Gallery talks and cultural programs with a warm palette.
cover: Build one high-contrast block of type low on the slide.
content: Use generous upper negative space and small catalog captions.

name: Boxed Graphic
use: Confident design critique with a graphic frame.
cover: Put the title in a strong border with an off-axis color tile.
content: Switch partition sizes to isolate an image, critique prompt or project outcome.

name: Clear Blue
use: Clear internal decisions and client reports.
cover: Start with one claim beside a framed or cropped image.
content: Use aligned rows for evidence, implications and decisions. Use fine blue rules.

name: Street Poster
use: Direct, high-energy statements and design launches.
cover: Let the headline occupy a broad rectangle and anchor it with one color cut.
content: Give every evidence slide one oversize visual or one statement.

name: Evening Dispatch
use: News-style analysis and consequential stories.
cover: Use a strong headline above a wide single image.
content: Frame the story with short column blocks, subheads and one deliberate divider.

name: Round Forms
use: Small-product launches and approachable workshop materials.
cover: Balance one rounded graphic with short stacked lines.
content: Use pill forms to contain brief categories. Keep longer explanations in open space.

name: Coordinate Paper
use: Quiet design research and structured essays.
cover: Align a minimal headline to light coordinate marks.
content: Anchor observations to a precise, legible diagram and put annotations outside the data.

name: Blue Graph
use: Analytical design research and modernist study decks.
cover: Use a strict left grid and one cropped blue form.
content: Align chart axes, captions and figures across pages.

name: Coral Cut
use: Warm product stories with confident color use.
cover: Place the title against a coral color plane and a material detail.
content: Keep color blocks large and captions understated.

name: Studio Margin
use: Design reviews driven by hands-on work.
cover: Show a work image over a large-print headline crop.
content: Use simple color strips to distinguish hypotheses, sketches and decisions.

name: Sunny Lesson
use: Friendly lessons and public workshops.
cover: Pair the learning goal with one bright radial mark.
content: Use ample margins and rounded image frames. Present one activity per slide.

name: Woodland Notes
use: Reflective research and storytelling with a photo-led atmosphere.
cover: Let the title sit beside a believable field detail.
content: Alternate full-scene moments with readable cream-on-green findings.

name: Warm Three Tone
use: Editorial stories with three restrained color roles.
cover: Introduce a large image and a small warm accent region.
content: Give background, type and annotations consistent color meanings.

name: Green Cover
use: Confident editorial introductions and formal creative reviews.
cover: Frame the headline and crop a portrait or detail within one large box.
content: Move long reading into balanced columns with warm light type.

name: Field Journal
use: Field observations, nature stories and research records.
cover: Pair a quiet title with a small drawn trace and a full-context photo.
content: Use consistent edge captions for location, change and evidence.

name: Long Table Stories
use: People-centered gatherings and warm workshop stories.
cover: Give the lead photograph a low, wide crop and space around the title.
content: Use adjacent quote and image shapes and attribute observations in notes.

name: Material Board
use: Tactile materials, packaging and deliberate product craft.
cover: Center the subject on a thick paper-like matte beside the title.
content: Use aligned samples, three variations and short descriptors.

name: Archive Ledger
use: Neutral archives, exhibits and text-centered reports.
cover: Use quiet typography, discrete rules and a generous front margin.
content: Compose source evidence with numbered rows, page rhythm and monochrome imagery.

name: Modular Contrast
use: Confident systems and editorial grids.
cover: Anchor one bold title to a large structured tile.
content: Arrange visual evidence on clear module boundaries aligned with text.

name: Community Billboard
use: Community announcements and calls to action.
cover: Use a short, high-contrast statement with a strong horizontal edge.
content: Show real actions prominently and put requests in plain language.

name: Pinned Pages
use: Hands-on research and desk-based evidence.
cover: Set a crisp document or photo on a matte with a modest pin detail.
content: Use photo pairs, handwriting fragments and clear typed captions.

name: Rose After Dark
use: Night events and warm, intimate editorial stories.
cover: Put an italic accent in a minimal title beside a dim color halo.
content: Use deep fields, a soft photo edge and consistent light captions.

name: Friendly Cutouts
use: Friendly small-team demos and playful activity decks.
cover: Hold the title together with two simple cutout shapes.
content: Use paired illustration and caption panels with generous inter-panel space.

name: Industrial Grid
use: Direct industrial design and system explanations.
cover: Use a tight, scale-driven title and a wide block at the edge.
content: Give each chart and photo an equal grid baseline and fine figure labels.

name: Retro Panels
use: Nostalgic desktop-style stories and playful technical lessons.
cover: Use generic framed panels and thin title bars with an original proportion.
content: Keep decorative chrome outside data and avoid copying a named interface.

name: Cut and Print
use: Handmade exhibition notes and community research.
cover: Use a boxy headline and a small printed image offset.
content: Combine aligned captions with one irregular crop or annotation per page.

name: Rose Catalog
use: Playful tactile product catalogs and live showcases.
cover: Reserve half the stage for the actual device and a small pixel motif.
content: Group details by use. Keep cropped product photos legible.

name: Idea Wall
use: Sprint facilitation and warm workshop stories.
cover: Anchor the title into an orderly composition of a few note colors.
content: Show the actual group activity and label one result for each visual cluster.

name: Institutional Mark
use: Formal recommendations and institutional briefings.
cover: Use moderate type and a compact geometric stamp.
content: Put evidence and decision beside a quiet, stable marginal rule.

name: Soft Review
use: Calm editorial reviews and small-room research talks.
cover: Use a modestly scaled title with a strong reading baseline.
content: Support the story with one unbroken image region and an unobtrusive caption.

name: Pressed Matter
use: Archival objects, wayfinding studies and material histories.
cover: Frame intense type in a warm block and leave one edge open.
content: Use orderly artifact placement, earthy lines and compact numerical notes.

name: Electric Stage
use: A high-impact keynote or design reveal.
cover: Set a broad graphic headline against a crisp right-angle field.
content: Give transitions a quick decisive movement and keep evidence still once shown.

name: Scholarly Night
use: Scholarly argument and evening discussions.
cover: Build a calm headline with a small accent mark near a deep reading plane.
content: Use restrained columns, figure notes and comfortable line lengths.
